previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with epistaxis, hypotension, and acute blood loss anemia, with a hemoglobin of 8.1 g/dL and hematocrit nadir of 20.8%. The bleeding was multifactorial, attributed to gastritis confirmed by EGD, ongoing epistaxis, and anticoagulation with warfarin. He received a total of 8 units of packed red blood cells. Warfarin and aspirin were held initially, with bridging anticoagulation using heparin infusion, later resumed at 2 mg daily as INR normalized. Pantoprazole was increased to twice daily for gastritis management. Transfusion-related fluid overload led to mild pulmonary congestion, managed with a single dose of IV furosemide; his home diuretic regimen was then resumed. He stabilized hemodynamically, with resolution of bleeding and improved symptoms, and was discharged home with home health services and follow-up arranged with PCP, ENT, and hematology.

setting of epistaxis and melena; the patient was managed
